headline: US government bonds rallied on Thursday as investors ran from AI-linked stocks and credit, even after a hot inflation reading.
score_reason: Clear, sourced bond-market move linked to the AI sell-off; one outlet read, so status REPORTED.
importance_line: Government bonds are acting as a safe haven again, which eases borrowing costs for households and governments, but the move reflects fear about AI company debt and growth rather than calm, and BigGo's account rests on market data it does not source in full.
summary: BigGo Finance reports that the 10-year US Treasury yield fell about 15 basis points to roughly 5.04% on Thursday 15 Oct 2026, its lowest since 23 Sep, as fears over AI financing costs outweighed the fastest rise in producer prices in more than four years. A falling yield means rising bond prices; BlackRock, the world's largest asset manager, cut US stocks to neutral and raised its view of Treasuries this week.
notes: The Financial Times original (Treasuries rally as investors seek shelter from AI turbulence) returned 403; BigGo Finance's report on the same Thursday rally was read instead and credited. Not copied from the FT.
